case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh and another v Bheru Singh and another
petitioner: State of Madhya Pradesh and another
respondent:
Bheru Singh and another
Supreme Court of India

1 February 2012
CIVIL APPEAL NO._1211 OF 2012 (Arising out of SLP (C) 30685 of 2009)WITH CIVIL  APPEAL NO. 1212 OF 2012 (Arising out of SLP (C ) No. 10163/2010
The Judgment was delivered by: Gyan Sudha Misra, J.
1. Leave granted.
2. These two appeals arise out of the judgement and order dated 11.08.2009 passed by the High Court of Madhya Pradesh, Bench at Indore in a public interest petition bearing Writ Petition No. 48 of 2004 against which the State of Madhya Pradesh as also the respondents Bheru Singh alongswith two
facts: The material factual details of these two appeals have a prolonged history giving rise to a labyrinth of litigation which emerged as a consequence of displacement of large number of persons from a massive area of agricultural and homestead land which were in occupation of the oustees/displaced persons, due to land acquisition which was done for the purpose of construction of Man Dam on the tributary of Narmada River in the State of Madhya Pradesh.
A Rehabilitation and Re-settlement (R & R) was framed by the State of M.P. for the project affected families (PAF) and oustees of Narmada Project including 'Man Dam'.
In order to resolve the same, the Government of Madhya Pradesh constituted a Committee known as Grievance Redressal Authority.
The intention behind the approval of SRG was that every oustees' level of living should not be lower than what it was before displacement, even if they cannot be made better off.
Out of 448 families, 386 families accepted the full cash compensation as per R & R Policy and remaining 62 who demanded land, have been allotted land in the year 1994 itself.

Thereafter, on 1.5.2009, the State of Madhya Pradesh filed further affidavit in the writ petition No. 48/2004 wherein it was clarified that the cash compensation was given to the land holders in 1995 with the direction to the bank to initially disburse only 50 per cent of the amount , with the balance 50 per cent being payable only after obtaining an order in that behalf from the concerned Land Acquisition Officer.

The Hon'ble High Court vide its impugned order dated 11.8.2009 passed in W.P.No.48/2004 was pleased to hold that there was substantial compliance of R & R Policy but by relying on a previous judgment and order dated 21.2.2008 passed by the High Court of M.P. in W.P.No.4457/2007 (Narmada Bachao Andolan vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 2011 Indlaw SC 462) directed the State to allotland to the adult son irrespective of the fact whether he had lost the land or not.
issues: What is the scope and meaning of 'substantial compliance' in the context of rehabilitation and resettlement policies?
Is the State's policy on providing land to displaced families violative of fundamental rights under Article 21 of the Constitution?
Can the State be directed to pay Special Rehabilitation Grant (SRG) amount on the basis of average sale price of the year 2001-02, this being a policy matter?
petitioner_arguments: The respondents were not entitled to deduct the amount of compensation payable for trees and wells located on the land of oustees as determined under the award passed under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 from the SRG amount paid to the oustees.
Woman who are included in the definition of 'displaced persons' will be given those benefits under the Rehabilitation Policy by the Respondents which are to be given to 'displaced persons'.
respondent_arguments: The State has substantially complied with the rehabilitation and resettlement policy for the displaced families.
The adult sons are not entitled for allotment of land as per the R & R Policy.
The definition of 'displaced family' in paragraph 1(b) of the Rehabilitation Policy does not discriminate against women and is not violative of Arts. 14 and 21 of the Constitution.
court_reasoning: The Hon'ble High Court vide its impugned order dated 11.8.2009 passed in W.P.No.48/2004 was pleased to hold that there was substantial compliance of R & R Policy but by relying on a previous judgment and order dated 21.2.2008 passed by the High Court of M.P. in W.P.No.4457/2007 (Narmada Bachao Andolan vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 2011 Indlaw SC 462) directed the State to allotland to the adult son irrespective of the fact whether he had lost the land or not.

The three Judge Bench of the Supreme Court by its judgment and order dated 11.5.2011 passed in Civil Appeal No. 2082/2011 reported in (2011) 7 SCC 639 2011 Indlaw SC 332 set aside the judgment and order dated 21.2.2008 passed in W.P.No.4457/2007 and held that the adult sons are not entitled for allotment of land as per the R & R Policy.
holding: The High Court directed the State to allotland to the adult son irrespective of the fact whether he had lost the land or not.
The Supreme Court set aside the judgment and order dated 21.2.2008 passed in W.P.No.4457/2007 and held that the adult sons are not entitled for allotment of land as per the R & R Policy.
